claim: The human nervous system contains at least hundreds of distinct subtypes of neurons that are necessary to create complex circuits.
source: The human nervous system contains at least hundreds of distinct subtypes of neurons that are necessary to create complex circuits.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the nervous system.

claim: Known extracellular trophic factor cocktails do not enable sufficient control and specificity to efficiently reprogram progenitor populations to a desired differentiated state.
source: Significant effort has shown that known extracellular trophic factor cocktails, although useful, do not enable sufficient control and specificity to efficiently reprogram progenitor populations to a desired differentiated state (Kriks et al., 2011; Maroof et al., 2013; Shi et al., 2012a; Shi et al., 2012b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple published studies.

claim: Yamanaka demonstrated the potential of transcription factor-based reprogramming by reprogramming somatic cells to pluripotency.
source: In fact, the pioneering work of Yamanaka demonstrated the potential of such an approach by reprogramming somatic cells to pluripotency (Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the Yamanaka study.

claim: Cell fate decisions during neurogenesis are mediated through the unique and highly coordinated temporal and spatial expression of hundreds of transcription factors.
source: Although neurons inherit the same genes, cell fate decisions during neurogenesis are mediated through the unique and highly coordinated temporal and spatial expression of hundreds of transcription factors.
evidence: This is a statement based on established scientific knowledge about neurogenesis.

claim: Plasmid or non-replicative viral vectors afford only crude temporal control over transcription factor levels and stoichiometries while depending on a proliferative cellular state.
source: However, this approach has severe limitations: (1) it affords only crude temporal control over transcription factor levels and stoichiometries while depending on a proliferative cellular state, (2) the copy numbers delivered to the cells are highly variable, and (3) the use of any DNA or integrative viral vector entails the risk of integration-induced mutagenesis leading to functional genetic alterations.
evidence: This is a statement of known limitations of DNA-based delivery methods.

claim: The copy numbers delivered to cells by plasmid or non-replicative viral vectors are highly variable.
source: However, this approach has severe limitations: (1) it affords only crude temporal control over transcription factor levels and stoichiometries while depending on a proliferative cellular state, (2) the copy numbers delivered to the cells are highly variable, and (3) the use of any DNA or integrative viral vector entails the risk of integration-induced mutagenesis leading to functional genetic alterations.
evidence: This is a statement of known limitations of DNA-based delivery methods.

claim: The use of DNA or integrative viral vectors entails the risk of integration-induced mutagenesis leading to functional genetic alterations.
source: However, this approach has severe limitations: (1) it affords only crude temporal control over transcription factor levels and stoichiometries while depending on a proliferative cellular state, (2) the copy numbers delivered to the cells are highly variable, and (3) the use of any DNA or integrative viral vector entails the risk of integration-induced mutagenesis leading to functional genetic alterations.
evidence: This is a statement of known risks associated with DNA-based delivery methods.

claim: In vitro synthesized mRNAs represent an important alternative to the use of DNA vectors.
source: In vitro synthesized mRNAs represent an important alternative to the use of DNA vectors (Karikó et al., 2005; Karikó and Weissman, 2007; Karikó et al., 2008; Angel and Yanik, 2010; Karikó et al., 2012; Kormann et al., 2011; Mandal and Rossi, 2013; Warren et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Suppressing the innate immune response enables high expression levels of transcription factors in cells with repeated mRNA delivery while avoiding the risk of genomic insertion.
source: By suppressing the innate immune response to reduce the toxicity of exogenous RNA, we have previously been able to achieve high expression levels of transcription factors in cells with repeated delivery while avoiding the risk of genomic insertion (Angel and Yanik, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: The lifetime of mRNA is shorter than that of DNA-based vectors, allowing more precise temporal control of transfected RNAs.
source: In addition, since the lifetime of mRNA is shorter than that of DNA-based vectors, the temporal availability of transfected RNAs can be much more precisely controlled over repeated delivery.
evidence: This is a statement based on known properties of mRNA versus DNA.

claim: Testing all possible stoichiometries and temporal delivery patterns of transcription factors would far exceed the capabilities of existing laboratories using 96- or 384-well plate formats.
source: Although several transcription factor libraries exist, and significant amounts of microarray and in situ hybridization data are now available, even for the relatively well-studied neuron types, testing all possible stoichiometries and temporal delivery patterns of transcription factors suspected to be involved in lineage specification would far exceed the capabilities of existing laboratories and technologies that use even large-scale formats such as 96- or 384- well plates.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combinatorial complexity of the problem.

claim: The magnetically-guided spotting platform focuses transcription factors onto 1.5 mm spots using dynamically reconfigurable magnetic-field patterns.
source: By focusing transcription factors onto 1.5 mm spots using dynamically reconfigurable magnetic-field patterns, we significantly reduced the footprint of the experiments to enable screening of transcription factor cocktails over large combinatorial spaces.
evidence: This describes the technical approach developed in this study.

claim: With the magnetically-guided spotting platform, the amount of RNA and transfection reagent required for a given transcription factor is proportional only to the number of spots actually transfected with that factor, rather than to the total number of possible spots in the array.
source: Importantly, with our technology the amount of RNA and transfection reagent required for a given transcription factor is proportional only to the number of spots actually transfected with that factor, rather than to the total number of possible spots in the array (i.e. to the surface area of transfected cells, not to the total surface area of the plate).
evidence: This describes a key feature of the technology developed in this study.

claim: The number of cell medium changes scales linearly with the number of transcription factors delivered, rather than growing exponentially with the number of combinatorial possibilities.
source: The number of cell medium changes we use also scale linearly with the number of transcription factors delivered, rather than growing exponentially with the number of combinatorial possibilities.
evidence: This describes an efficiency advantage of the technology.

claim: Testing every possible combination of 5 transcription factors results in 31 unique conditions but requires only 5 medium changes when the magnetically-guided spotting platform is used.
source: For example, testing every possible combination of just 5 transcription factors results in 31 unique conditions (i.e. all 5 factors alone, 10 possible 2-factor cocktails, 10 possible 3-factor cocktails, 5 possible 4-factor cocktails, and 1 possible 5-factor cocktail) but requires only 5 medium changes when our platform is used.
evidence: This is a calculation demonstrating the efficiency of the platform.

claim: The mRNA template was constructed with a T7 promoter and engineered with untranslated regions (UTRs) of highly stable Human β–globin (Hbb) at both 5' and 3' ends.
source: The mRNA template was constructed with a T7 promoter and was engineered with untranslated regions (UTRs) of highly stable Human β–globin (Hbb) at both 5' and 3' ends (Angel and Yanik, 2010), since UTRs play a significant role in mRNA stability (Yu and Russell, 2001; Jiang et al., 2006).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and is shown in Figure 1a. The rationale is supported by citations.

claim: UTRs play a significant role in mRNA stability.
source: The mRNA template was constructed with a T7 promoter and was engineered with untranslated regions (UTRs) of highly stable Human β–globin (Hbb) at both 5' and 3' ends (Angel and Yanik, 2010), since UTRs play a significant role in mRNA stability (Yu and Russell, 2001; Jiang et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Magnetofection yields faster and higher transfection efficiencies than most lipid-based transfection methods, especially for hard-to-transfect cell types such as primary neurons.
source: Magnetofection has been used for DNA and RNA transfection of cultured cells and yields faster and higher transfection efficiencies than most lipid-based transfection methods, especially for hard-to-transfect cell types such as primary neurons (Sapet et al., 2011; Plank et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Standard transfection approaches rely on stochastic diffusion and collision of transfection reagents with cells, which is a slow process that transfects cells non-specifically over the entire surface of the cell culture plate.
source: Standard transfection approaches rely on stochastic diffusion and collision of transfection reagents with cells, which is a slow process that transfects cells non-specifically over the entire surface of the cell culture plate (leftmost panels in Figure 1b and Figure 1c).
evidence: This describes a limitation of standard methods and is illustrated in Figure 1b and 1c.

claim: Standard magnetofection using a single magnet results in partial transfection of cells that lie outside the target area due to the non-uniform nature of the magnetic field.
source: However, due to the non-uniform nature of the magnetic field around a single magnet, magnetofection of cells is not spatially limited by the magnet's physical boundaries and therefore results in partial transfection of cells that lie outside the target area (middle panels in Figure 1b and Figure 1c).
evidence: This describes a limitation of standard magnetofection and is shown in Figure 1b and 1c.

claim: The dual-magnet configuration enables spatially restricted transfection of cells with minimal background transfection outside the boundaries of the magnets.
source: To overcome these limitations, we first introduce a simple dual-magnet configuration which focuses the magnetic field to millimeter-size spots in between pairs of magnets positioned above and below the surface of the plate with opposite poles facing one another (rightmost panel in Figure 1b). This configuration enables spatially restricted transfection of cells with minimal background transfection outside the boundaries of the magnets (rightmost panels in Figure 1c).
evidence: This describes a key innovation of the study and is demonstrated in Figure 1b and 1c.

claim: Neodymium (NdFeB) rare-earth magnets possess high magnetic anisotropy and high magnetic coercivity.
source: They possess high magnetic anisotropy (i.e. they preferentially align their magnetic moment along an 'easy' axis) and high magnetic coercivity (the ability to resist demagnetisation under an external magnetic field).
evidence: This is a statement of known physical properties of NdFeB magnets.

claim: Alnico five magnets and electromagnets were found to be inadequate due to insufficient magnetic field or failure to withstand demagnetisation.
source: In addition to NdFeB magnets, we tested Alnico five magnets and electromagnets and found both to be inadequate due to insufficient magnetic field (electromagnet; B ~ 10 mT) or failure to withstand demagnetisation (Alnico 5).
evidence: This describes experimental testing of alternative magnet types.

claim: The strength of the magnetic field was measured ~500 mT on the surface of top magnets.
source: The strength of the magnetic field was measured ~500 mT on the surface of top magnets.
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the study.

claim: The magnetic field density on the surface of each bottom magnet is B ~ 300 mT in isolation and B ~ 100 mT when inside the array.
source: The magnetic field density on the surface of each magnet is B ~ 300 mT in isolation and B ~ 100 mT when inside the array.
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the study.

claim: GFP-transfected spots of proliferating and differentiating NPCs remain isolated from each other even after 7 days post-transfection.
source: However, Figure 1f shows that the GFP-transfected spots of proliferating and differentiating NPCs remain isolated from each other even after 7 days post-transfection and our results in the subsequent sections show the stability of differentiated cell spots even after 17 days (i.e. when the differentiation protocol is completed).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1f.

claim: The magnetically-guided spotting platform delivers 0.6 ng of mRNA per 1.5 mm diameter spot (total surface area per spot: ~1.8 mm2).
source: Unless otherwise noted, we deliver 0.6 ng of mRNA per 1.5 mm diameter spot (total surface area per spot: ~1.8 mm2) for all of our experiments.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol used in the study.

claim: Achieving a comparable level of transfection in a 96-well format requires ~18 fold more reagents than the magnetically-guided spotting platform.
source: Achieving a comparable level of transfection in a 96-well format (total surface area per well: ~32.2 mm2) requires ~18 fold more reagents.
evidence: This is a calculation comparing reagent requirements between methods.

claim: Small multiwell assays (384- or 1536-well plates) suffer significantly from variation due to edge effects.
source: Although the reagent requirements for multiwell plate screens can be further reduced with 384- or 1536-well plate assays, these smaller formats suffer significantly from variation due to edge effects, which also cause problems for even 96-well screens (Lundholt et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: DNA-based delivery methods are vulnerable to low/variable efficiency because transfected molecules must cross both the plasma membrane and the nuclear envelope.
source: DNA-based delivery methods are most vulnerable to low/variable efficiency because transfected molecules must be transcribed in order to be effective and therefore must cross both the plasma membrane and the nuclear envelope.
evidence: This is an explanation based on known biological mechanisms.

claim: mRNA-based methods tend to yield much higher transfection efficiencies since transfected molecules need to cross only the plasma membrane to be expressed.
source: In contrast, mRNA-based methods tend to yield much higher transfection efficiencies since transfected molecules need to cross only the plasma membrane to be expressed.
evidence: This is an explanation based on known biological mechanisms.

claim: A comparison of plasmid- and mRNA-based transfection approaches in human embryonic stem cell-derived retinal pigmented epithelial cells shows that DNA efficiency is only ~10% while RNA efficiency is ~90%.
source: For example, a comparison of plasmid- and mRNA-based transfection approaches in human embryonic stem cell-derived retinal pigmented epithelial cells shows that DNA efficiency is only ~10% while RNA efficiency is ~90% (Hansson et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: An extensive comparison of DNA and RNA transfection protocols using immature dendritic cells suggests that DNA-based approaches can achieve transfection efficiencies of 10–20% whereas RNA-based approaches can achieve efficiencies of 40–80%.
source: Similarly, an extensive comparison of DNA and RNA transfection protocols using immature dendritic cells suggests that DNA-based approaches can achieve transfection efficiencies of 10–20% whereas RNA-based approaches can achieve efficiencies of 40–80% (Landi et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: Interleaved transfection (four transfections of 8 ng each) results in more uniform cell-to-cell expression compared to single transfection (one transfection of 32 ng) when delivering the same total amount of mRNA (64 ng).
source: Human neural progenitor cells were cultured in 12-well plates and spotted with mRNAs encoding GFP (Green) or mCherry (Red) using either a standard single transfection process (32 ng of each mRNA) or a quadruple transfection protocol (four transfections consisting of 8 ng of each mRNA per transfection). In both cases the total amount of mRNA delivered to the spots was 64 ng and the medium was changed after each transfection. As shown in Figure 2b, although both methods result in a majority of all cells being transfected, cell-to-cell expression is considerably more variable when using the single-transfection method.
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally and shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Interleaved transfection improves the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) to 0.85 and Mander's overlap coefficient (MOC) to 0.92, compared to single transfection which results in PCC of 0.54 and MOC of 0.79.
source: Although a single transfection results in co-localization (PCC >0.5) with 79% overlap (MOC = 0.79), interleaved transfection improves the PCC to 0.85 and MOC to 0.92, which is indicative of highly uniform and co-localized transfection of cells with both mRNAs.
evidence: This is quantitative data from the experiment shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Precise dosage control and transfection gradients can be achieved using the magnetically-guided spotting platform.
source: Precise dosage control and transfection gradients can be achieved as shown in Figure 2d where NPCs were spotted with GFP and mCherry mRNAs at three different dosages horizontally and vertically, respectively.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2d.

claim: Parkinson's disease is one of the most common neurodegenerative disorders resulting from the functional loss of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra pars compacta of midbrain.
source: Parkinson's disease is one of the most common neurodegenerative disorders resulting from the functional loss of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra pars compacta of midbrain (Lees et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established medical knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Deriving sufficiently pure cultures of dopaminergic neurons remains a key challenge.
source: However, deriving sufficiently pure cultures of dopaminergic neurons remains a key challenge.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of the field.

claim: The study screened a pool of midbrain-specific transcription factors (OTX2, LMX1A, FOXA2, ASCL1, NGN2, NURR1, and PITX3) reported in the literature to be involved in either the fate specification, survival, or maintenance of ventral midbrain dopaminergic cells.
source: We used proliferative NPCs, due to their relative ease to expand and culture as monolayers in the presence of growth factor mitogens (bFGF and EGF), and conducted the screen using a pool of midbrain-specific transcription factors reported in the literature to be involved in either the fate specification, survival, or maintenance of ventral midbrain dopaminergic cells (OTX2, LMX1A, FOXA2, ASCL1, NGN2, NURR1, and PITX3) (Hegarty et al., 2013; Abeliovich and Hammond, 2007; Ang, 2006).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and is supported by citations.

claim: OTX2, ASCL1, and NGN2 are essential during early neural development for the correct positioning of isthmus organizer and the development of the midbrain.
source: While OTX2, ASCL1, and NGN2 are essential during early neural development for the correct positioning of isthmus organizer and the development of the midbrain (Martinez-Barbera et al., 2001; Puelles et al., 2003; Kele et al., 2006), FOXA2 and LMX1A are necessary for the correct positioning of dopaminergic cell types along the ventral-caudal axis of the midbrain (Nakatani et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: FOXA2 and LMX1A are necessary for the correct positioning of dopaminergic cell types along the ventral-caudal axis of the midbrain.
source: While OTX2, ASCL1, and NGN2 are essential during early neural development for the correct positioning of isthmus organizer and the development of the midbrain (Martinez-Barbera et al., 2001; Puelles et al., 2003; Kele et al., 2006), FOXA2 and LMX1A are necessary for the correct positioning of dopaminergic cell types along the ventral-caudal axis of the midbrain (Nakatani et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: PITX3 has been shown to be expressed in all dopaminergic neurons in the CNS during maturation and, together with NURR1, is necessary for their survival and maintenance.
source: PITX3 has been shown to be expressed in all dopaminergic neurons in the CNS during maturation and, together with NURR1, is necessary for their survival and maintenance (Saucedo-Cardenas et al., 1998; Peng et al., 2011; Martinat et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Among spots transfected during induction stage, LMX1A (LmI) was the only factor that significantly increased the yield of TH+ neurons on its own (p<0.01, 40 ± 5% TH+/MAP2+ cells compared to the control, 22 ± 4%).
source: Interestingly, among spots transfected during induction stage, LMX1A (LmI) was the only factor that significantly increased the yield of TH+ neurons on its own (p<0.01, 40 ± 5% TH+/MAP2+ cells compared to the control, 22 ± 4%).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study shown in Figure 3b and 3d.

claim: Significantly more TH+ neurons were counted in spots transfected during the NPC stage with either FOXA2 (FoN) (TH+/MAP2+, 27 ± 4%, p<0.05), PITX3 (PtN) (TH+/MAP2+, 35 ± 3%, p<0.01), or LMX1A (LmN) (TH+/MAP2+, 32 ± 3%, p<0.01).
source: On the other hand, significantly more TH+ neurons were counted in spots transfected during the NPC stage with either FOXA2 (FoN) (TH+/MAP2+, 27 ± 4%, p<0.05), PITX3 (PtN) (TH+/MAP2+, 35 ± 3%, p<0.01), or LMX1A (LmN) (TH+/MAP2+, 32 ± 3%, p<0.01), albeit with less effect than post-induction transfection with LMX1A (LmI) (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study shown in Figure 3b.

claim: FOXA2 and PITX3 are more efficient when delivered to NPCs whereas LMX1A is more efficient when delivered during induction of differentiation after mitogen removal.
source: These results suggest that FOXA2 and PITX3 are more efficient when delivered to NPCs whereas LMX1A is more efficient when delivered during induction of differentiation after mitogen removal.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Direct overexpression of OTX2, ASCL1, or NGN2 did not increase TH+ neurons in the experiment.
source: Although OTX2, ASCL1, NGN2 are thought to play a role in dopaminergic differentiation, in our experiment their direct overexpression did not increase TH+ neurons.
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: Triple combination of FoN +PtN + LmI produced significantly more TH+ cells (p<0.001, 68 ± 5% TH+/MAP2+) than any other combination.
source: Although all dual combinations increased the number of converted cells, triple combination of these factors (FoN +PtN + LmI) produced significantly more TH+ cells (p<0.001, 68 ± 5% TH+/MAP2+) than any other combination (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Gene expression analysis at day 17 of differentiation confirms robust seven-fold over-expression of TH in response to the FoN +PtN + LmI triple combination of factors when compared to non-transfected cells.
source: Gene expression analysis at day 17 of differentiation (Figure 3e) confirms robust seven-fold over-expression of TH in response to the FoN +PtN + LmI triple combination of factors when compared to non-transfected cells.
evidence: This is experimental data from the study shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Neuronal identity (MAP2+) was observed in ~98% of both FoN +PtN + LmI transfected cells and the non-transfected controls.
source: Neuronal identity (MAP2+) was observed in ~98% of both FoN +PtN + LmI transfected cells and the non-transfected controls.
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: Transfected cells yielded significantly higher FOXA2+ neurons co-expressing TH (p<0.001, 75 ± 4%, TH+/FOXA2+) compared to non-transfected cells (30 ± 3% FOXA2+/TH+).
source: However, transfected cells yielded significantly higher FOXA2+ neurons co-expressing TH (p<0.001, 75 ± 4%, TH+/FOXA2+) compared to non-transfected cells (30 ± 3% FOXA2+/TH+).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Among the transfected transcription factors, LMX1A was up-regulated by eleven-fold, FOXA2 by nine-fold and PITX3 by five-fold 2 weeks after transfection with the FoN +PtN + LmI combination.
source: Among the transfected transcription factors, LMX1A was up-regulated by eleven-fold, FOXA2 by nine-fold and PITX3 by five-fold 2 weeks after transfection with the FoN +PtN + LmI combination.
evidence: This is experimental data from the study shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Two of the non-effective transcription factors used in the initial screen (OTX2 and NURR1) were up-regulated by eight- and four-fold respectively after transfection with the FoN +PtN + LmI combination.
source: Surprisingly, two of the non-effective transcription factors used in our initial screen (OTX2 and NURR1) were also up-regulated by eight- and four-fold respectively.
evidence: This is experimental data from the study shown in Figure 4c.

claim: VMAT2, a well-known midbrain regional marker expressed in substantia nigra DA neuron sub-types, was up-regulated by more than five-fold after transfection with the FoN +PtN + LmI combination.
source: A well-known midbrain regional marker expressed in substantia nigra DA neuron sub-types (VMAT2) was also up-regulated by more than five-fold, further confirming that our optimized triple combination of transcription factors (FoN +PtN + LmI) gives rise to dopaminergic neurons with midbrain identity.
evidence: This is experimental data from the study shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The optimized triple combination of transcription factors (FoN +PtN + LmI) gives rise to dopaminergic neurons with midbrain identity.
source: A well-known midbrain regional marker expressed in substantia nigra DA neuron sub-types (VMAT2) was also up-regulated by more than five-fold, further confirming that our optimized triple combination of transcription factors (FoN +PtN + LmI) gives rise to dopaminergic neurons with midbrain identity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on marker expression.

claim: Various yields and purities of dopaminergic neural differentiation from hPSCs and/or multipotent NPCs have been reported ranging from low (i.e. 10%) to high (80%).
source: Although various yields and purities of dopaminergic neural differentiation from hPSCs and/or mutipotent NPCs have been reported—ranging from low (i.e. 10%) to high (80%)—much of this variation can be attributed to differences in starting cell lines, growth factor cocktails, use of recombinant vs. purified proteins, cell purification procedures, and/or co-culture with other cells such as astrocytes (Engel et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a summary of literature findings supported by a citation.

claim: Much of the variation in reported dopaminergic differentiation efficiency can be attributed to differences in starting cell lines, growth factor cocktails, use of recombinant vs. purified proteins, cell purification procedures, and/or co-culture with other cells such as astrocytes.
source: Although various yields and purities of dopaminergic neural differentiation from hPSCs and/or mutipotent NPCs have been reported—ranging from low (i.e. 10%) to high (80%)—much of this variation can be attributed to differences in starting cell lines, growth factor cocktails, use of recombinant vs. purified proteins, cell purification procedures, and/or co-culture with other cells such as astrocytes (Engel et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference about the causes of variation, supported by a citation.

claim: The magnetically-guided spotting platform enables more accurate and quantitative comparisons by allowing many factors and conditions to be simultaneously tested side-by-side under the same laboratory conditions.
source: Our high-throughput magnetically-guided spotting platform, where many factors and conditions can be simultaneously tested side-by-side and compared under the same laboratory conditions, can in the future allow for more accurate and quantitative comparisons.
evidence: This is a claim about the potential future utility of the technology.

claim: Combinatorial delivery of LMX1A, FOXA2, and PITX3 is highly effective in generating dopaminergic neurons from neural progenitors.
source: We show that combinatorial delivery of LMX1A, FOXA2, and PITX3 is highly effective in generating dopaminergic neurons from neural progenitors, with LMX1A significantly increasing TH-expression levels when delivered during both the proliferating NPC stage and in the early neural induction stages upon mitogen withdrawal, while FOXA2 and PITX3 only exhibit high efficacy before neural induction.
evidence: This is a summary of the main experimental findings of the study.

claim: LMX1A significantly increases TH-expression levels when delivered during both the proliferating NPC stage and in the early neural induction stages upon mitogen withdrawal.
source: We show that combinatorial delivery of LMX1A, FOXA2, and PITX3 is highly effective in generating dopaminergic neurons from neural progenitors, with LMX1A significantly increasing TH-expression levels when delivered during both the proliferating NPC stage and in the early neural induction stages upon mitogen withdrawal, while FOXA2 and PITX3 only exhibit high efficacy before neural induction.
evidence: This is a summary of the main experimental findings of the study.

claim: FOXA2 and PITX3 only exhibit high efficacy before neural induction.
source: We show that combinatorial delivery of LMX1A, FOXA2, and PITX3 is highly effective in generating dopaminergic neurons from neural progenitors, with LMX1A significantly increasing TH-expression levels when delivered during both the proliferating NPC stage and in the early neural induction stages upon mitogen withdrawal, while FOXA2 and PITX3 only exhibit high efficacy before neural induction.
evidence: This is a summary of the main experimental findings of the study.

claim: The H9-derived human neural progenitor cell line (hNP1) has been validated for high levels of expression of Nestin and Sox2 and low level expression of Oct4.
source: Each lot of ENStem-ATM Human Neural Progenitor Cells has been validated for high levels of expression of Nestin and Sox2 and low level expression of Oct4.
evidence: This is information about the cell line used, provided by the manufacturer.

claim: The ability of ENStem-ATM cells to differentiate into multiple neuronal phenotypes and maintain a normal karyotype after multiple passages has been verified by the manufacturer.
source: The ability of ENStem-ATM cells to differentiate into multiple neuronal phenotypes and maintain a normal karyotype after multiple passages has been verified by the manufacturer, and the cells have been confirmed to be negative for mycoplasma.
evidence: This is information about the cell line used, provided by the manufacturer.

claim: The dual-magnet configuration focuses the magnetic field to millimeter-size spots in between pairs of magnets positioned above and below the surface of the plate with opposite poles facing one another.
source: To overcome these limitations, we first introduce a simple dual-magnet configuration which focuses the magnetic field to millimeter-size spots in between pairs of magnets positioned above and below the surface of the plate with opposite poles facing one another (rightmost panel in Figure 1b).
evidence: This describes the technical design of the system shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The incubation time for magnetofection was 2 min per transfection.
source: The incubation time for magnetofection was 2 min per transfection.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol used in the study.

claim: The concentration of the mRNA complex was adjusted based on the number of spots to be transfected per well (0.6 ng RNA per 1.5 mm diameter spot), ensuring that each spot received an equivalent amount of mRNA.
source: The concentration of the mRNA complex was adjusted based on the number of spots to be transfected per well (0.6 ng RNA per 1.5 mm diameter spot), ensuring that each spot received an equivalent amount of mRNA.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol used in the study.

claim: The magnetically-guided spotting platform can massively parallelize the combinatorial transfection of nucleic acids to rapidly explore vast search spaces of transcription factor stoichiometries.
source: To overcome this bottleneck, we developed a technology (Figure 1) that can massively parallelize the combinatorial transfection of nucleic acids in order to rapidly explore vast search spaces of transcription factor stoichiometries and validated it in an RNA-based screen on human neural progenitor cells (NPCs).
evidence: This describes the capability of the technology developed in this study.

claim: The technology was validated in an RNA-based screen on human neural progenitor cells (NPCs).
source: To overcome this bottleneck, we developed a technology (Figure 1) that can massively parallelize the combinatorial transfection of nucleic acids in order to rapidly explore vast search spaces of transcription factor stoichiometries and validated it in an RNA-based screen on human neural progenitor cells (NPCs).
evidence: This describes the validation of the technology in this study.

claim: The interleaved RNA transfection technique dramatically reduces fluctuations in the delivered mRNA copy numbers and stoichiometries.
source: Thus, we also demonstrate here an interleaved RNA transfection technique that dramatically reduces fluctuations in the delivered mRNA copy numbers and stoichiometries.
evidence: This is a summary of one of the key findings of the study.

claim: The study evaluated the temporal contributions of transcription factor cocktails by treating human NPCs with them during the proliferative stage and/or during the induction of neurogenesis.
source: Using our magnetically-guided spotting platform and interleaved transfection protocol, we evaluated the temporal contributions of transcription factor cocktails by treating human NPCs with them during the proliferative stage and/or during the induction of neurogenesis (i.e. after mitogen withdrawal) to generate human dopaminergic neurons with high purity.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: The study generated human dopaminergic neurons with high purity using the magnetically-guided spotting platform and interleaved transfection protocol.
source: Using our magnetically-guided spotting platform and interleaved transfection protocol, we evaluated the temporal contributions of transcription factor cocktails by treating human NPCs with them during the proliferative stage and/or during the induction of neurogenesis (i.e. after mitogen withdrawal) to generate human dopaminergic neurons with high purity.
evidence: This is a summary of the main outcome of the study.

claim: The top magnetic plate is comprised of 12 large 22 mm diameter NdFeB disk magnets positioned in a 3 × 4 matrix.
source: The top magnetic plate is comprised of 12 large 22 mm diameter NdFeB disk magnets (Supplementary file 1) positioned in a 3 × 4 matrix.
